title: Add opt-in boxed bash wrapper
description:
## Objective
Add an opt-in boxed wrapper for Pi's built-in `bash` tool.

## Context
The user specifically likes pi-droid-styling's treatment of bash tool calls/output. This bead implements the Phase 1 built-in wrapper behind `blackbytes.ui.boxed_builtin_tools=true`, delegating execution to Pi's bash implementation and replacing only the renderers.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `src/tools/builtin-wrappers/bash.ts` and registration from a wrapper index.
- Render boxed bash call with `$` / `>` prompt markers and shell highlighting.
- Render partial/pending, collapsed tail preview, expanded capped output, and footer metadata (elapsed/timeout/word count where available).
- Strip Pi truncation notice lines from preview body.
Out of scope:
- Changing bash execution semantics, cwd handling, timeout behavior, or model-visible output.
- Wrapping other built-ins.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/builtin-wrappers/bash.ts`
- `src/tools/builtin-wrappers/index.ts`
- `src/handlers/index.ts`
- Tests under `src/tools/builtin-wrappers/__tests__/` or integration tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `boxed_builtin_tools` default is false.
- If wrapper registration fails, skip and preserve Pi core behavior.
- Collapsed preview should avoid processing entire huge output.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Result details may not include elapsed timing unless wrapper records or preserves it; footer should gracefully show `--` when unavailable.
- Must not interfere with read-renderer hashline behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `bash` wrapper registers only when `blackbytes.ui.boxed_builtin_tools=true`.
- `renderCall` shows boxed multi-line command with `$` / `>` markers and shell highlighting.
- Collapsed result shows tail preview with long-line clamp and truncation notice filtering.
- Expanded result respects configured output caps and shows footer metadata for elapsed/timeout/word count when available.

## Validation / Definition of Done

title: Implement boxed render primitives
description:
## Objective
Implement reusable boxed tool rendering primitives in `src/tools/_shared/boxed-render.ts`.

## Context
Blackbytes tools currently use simple one-line renderers or custom per-tool result renderers. This bead creates the shared visual foundation for Phase 1 so later beads can migrate tools without duplicating frame/wrap/footer logic.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add boxed call/result helpers, compact call helper, footer helper, status styling, width-aware wrapping, and theme-token usage.
- Support success, error, pending/partial, collapsed, and expanded states.
- Add unit tests for box width, wrapping, footer, and state rendering.
Out of scope:
- Migrating individual tools.
- Built-in bash wrapper.
- Adding runtime dependencies or hardcoded 24-bit color themes.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/_shared/boxed-render.ts` — new shared renderer module.
- `src/tools/_shared/__tests__/boxed-render.test.ts` — new tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- None. This is the foundation bottleneck for most other boxed UI beads.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Follow Biome style: 2-space indent, double quotes, ESM `.js` imports.
- Use Pi semantic theme tokens; do not scan theme files or copy pi-droid-styling theme extras.
- Use `Text`/component-compatible render APIs already used in the repo.
- Keep helpers pure/testable where practical.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Tests should assert semantic tokens via stub theme, not brittle ANSI snapshots.
- Avoid overly tall default boxes; compact one-line box should be available for calls.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `renderBoxedToolCall`, `renderCompactBoxedToolCall`, `renderBoxedToolResult`, and footer helpers exist and are exported.
- Helpers render success, error, pending/partial, collapsed, and expanded states using semantic theme tokens.

- No new runtime dependency or hardcoded theme scanner is introduced.

## Validation / Definition of Done

- Tests cover success/error/pending, collapsed/expanded, wrapping at narrow widths, and footer output.
- No new runtime dependency is added.

title: Implement shared tool-output utilities
description:
## Objective
Implement shared tool-output utilities in `src/tools/_shared/tool-output.ts`.

## Context
Boxed result renderers need consistent text extraction, line counting, word counting, truncation, tail preview, and Pi truncation notice handling. Centralizing this prevents each tool from reimplementing output parsing.

## Scope
In scope:
- Extract text from tool result content blocks.
- Count lines and approximate words.
- Clamp long lines.
- Strip trailing Pi notice lines such as `[Showing last ... Full output: ...]` from preview bodies.
- Provide tail-preview and expanded-line cap helpers.
Out of scope:
- Redaction/persistence/logging.
- Semantic parsing of command output.
- Changing model-visible tool content.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/_shared/tool-output.ts` — new utility module.
- `src/tools/_shared/__tests__/tool-output.test.ts` — new tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Depends on `Implement boxed render primitives` because helper shapes should support boxed result needs.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Collapsed bash preview should avoid splitting full huge outputs when a backward tail scan is enough.
- Keep functions dependency-free and deterministic.
- Numeric caps come from config defaults added later, but helpers should accept explicit limit arguments.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Empty text content and mixed non-text content must not crash.
- CRLF output should normalize predictably for rendering without altering original tool result content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tool result text extraction works for empty, single, and multiple text blocks.
- Tail preview and expanded cap helpers handle large output and long lines predictably.
- Pi truncation notice lines are stripped from preview bodies without altering original result content.
- Line and word count helpers are covered by tests.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Tests cover empty content, multi-text-block content, CRLF normalization, notice stripping, long-line clamping, word/line counts, tail preview, and expanded cap elision.
close_reason: Implemented shared tool-output utilities for text extraction, counts, preview caps, truncation notice filtering, and tests.

title: Implement shell command highlighter
description:
## Objective
Implement dependency-free shell command highlighting in `src/tools/_shared/shell-highlight.ts`.

## Context
The opt-in built-in bash wrapper should make command invocations easy to scan, similar to pi-droid-styling, without adding syntax-highlighting dependencies or evaluating shell text.

## Scope
In scope:
- Tokenize shell lines while preserving whitespace.
- Style commands, flags, path-like tokens, shell variables, operators, and comments using theme tokens.
- Fall back safely for unterminated quotes or unknown patterns.
Out of scope:
- Full shell grammar correctness.
- Highlighting bash output bodies.
- Adding dependencies or calling shell parsers.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/_shared/shell-highlight.ts` — new highlighter.
- `src/tools/_shared/__tests__/shell-highlight.test.ts` — new tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Depends on `Implement boxed render primitives` because it is consumed by boxed bash call rendering.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Lexical highlighter only; never execute/evaluate shell content.
- Use semantic tokens similar to existing theme usage (`syntaxVariable`, `syntaxKeyword`, `syntaxFunction`, `syntaxString`, `syntaxOperator`, `syntaxComment`) with graceful fallback.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Quoted strings, escaped characters, and shell operators can be tricky; tests should cover representative cases, not full POSIX shell grammar.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shell highlighter styles command names, flags, path-like args, shell variables, operators, redirects, and comments.
- Tokenization preserves whitespace and readable command text.
- Unterminated quotes or unsupported syntax do not throw and render a safe fallback.
- No parser/highlighter dependency is added.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unit tests verify token styling for `bun run test`, flags, paths, `$VAR`, `${VAR}`, `&&`, pipes, redirects, and comments.
- Unterminated quote returns readable unstyled or fallback-styled text rather than throwing.
close_reason: Implemented dependency-free shell command highlighter with token styling and fallback tests.

title: Extend config schema with boxed UI options
description:
## Objective

## Scope

- Clamp numeric limits according to the spec.
- Add schema/loader tests.
Out of scope:

- Adding command UI for changing these options.

- `src/config/__tests__/schema.test.ts` and/or loader tests.

title: Error code taxonomy + strict patch rejection
description:
## Objective
Replace free-text error strings in `hashline_edit` with a typed error code taxonomy, and harden the "strict patch" rejection so accidentally-included `LINE#ID|` prefixes or diff markers in `lines` fail loudly instead of being silently stripped.

## Context
The LLM cannot reliably branch on error semantics from free-text. A typed taxonomy (`E_BAD_REF`, `E_HASH_MISMATCH`, `E_NO_MATCH`, `E_MULTI_MATCH`, `E_INVALID_PATCH`, `E_OVERLAP`, `E_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `E_WRITE_FAILED`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_VERIFY_FAILED`) lets downstream tooling and prompt guidance switch on the leading code. Current `stripLineIdPrefix` silently fixes a model mistake — opposite of hashline's "strict anchors fail" philosophy and inconsistent with `pi-hashline-edit`.

## Scope
In scope:
- New file `src/tools/hashline-edit/errors.ts` exporting `ERROR_CODES` enum and `formatError(code, message, context?)` helper producing the canonical `[CODE] message\n<context>` string.
- Refactor every error string in `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` to use `formatError(...)`.
- Replace `stripLineIdPrefix` (currently at `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts:71`) with a `validateLines(lines: string[]): void` function (export from `errors.ts`) that throws — or returns a structured error the caller maps to `E_INVALID_PATCH` — for any line matching `/^\d+#[A-Z]{2}\|/`. The diff-marker heuristic (`/^[+-] /`) is intentionally NOT included to avoid false positives on legitimate Markdown / prose; the `LINE#ID|` prefix is by far the more common model mistake and is the only signal we reject.
- Add config flag `hashline_edit.strict_patch: boolean` (default `true`) in `src/config/schema.ts`. When `false`, fall back to legacy strip-and-continue behaviour for backward compatibility.
- Update tool `description` and `promptGuidelines` to warn against including `LINE#ID|` prefix in the `lines` payload.
- New test `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/errors.test.ts` covering every code path (one positive case per code, plus strict_patch on/off).

Out of scope:
- Atomic write changes (T3) — `E_WRITE_FAILED` is reserved but only fired from existing `writeFileSync` for now.
- `E_VERIFY_FAILED` wiring (Phase 2 / T7) — code reserved, no trigger yet.
- `E_NO_MATCH` / `E_MULTI_MATCH` wiring (T4) — codes reserved, used by T4.
- Changing the response render layer.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — refactor all `error: ...` strings via `formatError`; swap `stripLineIdPrefix` for `validateLines`.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/errors.ts` (new) — taxonomy + helper.
- `src/config/schema.ts` — extend `hashline_edit` block with `strict_patch` default `true`.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/errors.test.ts` (new).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/hashline-edit.test.ts` — update assertions expecting prefix-strip to instead expect `E_INVALID_PATCH`; add `strict_patch=false` legacy case.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
None. This is the foundation task.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Config schema is `.passthrough()` (per `AGENTS.md`); adding `strict_patch` does not break existing settings files.
- Default `strict_patch=true` is a BREAKING semantic change for callers that relied on silent strip. Documented in CHANGELOG (handled in T6); escape via `strict_patch=false`.
- Error string format is `[CODE] <message>\n<optional context>` — the compactor at `index.ts:125-137` already handles long strings, keep it.
- `formatError(code, message, context?)` output shape: `"[CODE] <message>"` if no context; `"[CODE] <message>\n<context>"` if context provided. `context` is opaque — caller controls newline handling. The existing `compactHashlineError` (`index.ts:125-137`) operates on the final string and is unchanged.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Existing tests in `__tests__/hashline-edit.test.ts` likely assert silent strip behaviour. Update them to expect the new strict behaviour rather than weakening the new code.
- `validateLines` runs per-edit on `lines`; do not regress performance on large `lines: string[]` arrays. Use a single regex per line, no nested loops.
- The strict regex `/^\d+#[A-Z]{2}\|/` will also match a line whose 2 letters happen to be outside the CID alphabet (`ZPMQVRWSNKTXJBYH`) — e.g. `42#OL|...`. That is intentional: we reject on **shape**, not on alphabet membership, to keep the check fast and to flag any prefix-like artifact regardless of source. Document this in test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `errors.test.ts` covers all 10 codes (at least one positive case each).
- `hashline-edit.test.ts` updated; both `strict_patch=true` reject path and `strict_patch=false` legacy strip path covered.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` green.
- `formatError` output passes through `compactHashlineError` unchanged in length-bound tests.
close_reason: Implemented: error code taxonomy (10 codes in errors.ts), formatError + validateLines helpers, strict_patch=true default with strict_patch=false escape hatch via union config schema, refactored 8 error sites in index.ts. Added errors.test.ts (15 cases) + 3 new hashline-edit tests; updated 1 existing test. Lint/typecheck/test/build/size all green (673/673 tests).

title: Canonical-path mutation queue
description:
## Objective
Make `runQueuedHashlineEdit`'s per-file mutation queue canonical-path-aware so that concurrent edits arriving via different symlink paths to the same underlying file serialise on the same queue key.

## Context
`pi-blackbytes`'s queue currently keys on `input.filePath` literal. If two concurrent edits arrive — one through symlink `/repo/link.ts`, one through canonical `/real/file.ts` — they get separate `withFileMutationQueue` keys and race on the same inode. `pi-hashline-edit` resolves to canonical write target before queuing.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `safeRealpath(p: string): string` helper (export from `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts`). Returns `fs.realpathSync(p)` and falls back to `p` ONLY on `ENOENT`; all other errors rethrow so latent permission errors are not silently swallowed. T3 will reuse this export.
- In `runQueuedHashlineEdit` (`src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts:341-356`), map every entry of `queuePaths` through `safeRealpath` before `new Set(...)` deduplication and sort.
- Add a regression test that creates a real symlink under `os.tmpdir()`, fires two concurrent `applyHashlineEdits` via the runQueuedHashlineEdit entry (one via symlink path, one via canonical), and asserts the second sees the first's content (i.e. they serialised, no lost write).

Out of scope:
- Atomic write itself (T3).
- Changing the queue primitive — keep using `withFileMutationQueue` from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — modify `runQueuedHashlineEdit`; add helper.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/hashline-edit.test.ts` — add concurrent-symlink regression case (or extract into a dedicated `__tests__/canonical-queue.test.ts` if it ergonomically isolates the temp-dir fixture).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
None. Independent of T1.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `fs.realpathSync` does not throw for ENOENT on intermediate components only when the final component is missing; only catch `ENOENT` and rethrow other errors so latent permission errors do not get swallowed.
- The fallback to literal path on ENOENT is only correct for the **rename target** case — the source `filePath` is read shortly after queue acquisition, and if it does not exist it will produce an `E_NOT_FOUND` from the existing read step.
- Tests must clean up temp files in `afterEach` or via `os.tmpdir()` with random subdir.

## Risks / Gotchas
- On Windows, `fs.realpathSync` can normalise drive letter casing; assertions should compare normalised paths.
- Avoid resolving a path repeatedly inside the queued closure — resolve once at queue-key derivation time.
- Symlink test must skip on `process.platform === "win32"` (symlink creation requires elevated privileges by default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New concurrent-symlink regression test passes.
- `bun run test` shows the test serialising (assert second write sees first's content; in-place equality after both promises resolve).
- Existing tests all green.
close_reason: Implemented: exported safeRealpath(p) helper (ENOENT fallback, rethrows others); runQueuedHashlineEdit now canonicalises queue paths before set-dedup so symlink and canonical paths to the same inode serialise on the same key. Added canonical-queue.test.ts with 5 cases (safeRealpath + concurrent symlink race + rename ENOENT fallback). Windows-guarded with process.platform skip. 678/678 tests pass; lint/build/size green.

title: Atomic write + symlink/hardlink/permission preservation
description:
## Objective
Replace direct `writeFileSync` in `hashline_edit` with an atomic write helper that (a) writes via a temp file in the target's directory and renames over the canonical target, (b) preserves symlinks by writing to the resolved canonical path (not the symlink), (c) preserves hard-link inodes by writing in-place when `nlink > 1`, and (d) preserves the file mode bits.

## Context
A crash, kill, or disk-full event mid-write currently leaves the file truncated/corrupt. Plain `writeFileSync` also replaces a symlink with a regular file (silently breaking aliases) and breaks hard-link relationships by allocating a new inode on rename. `pi-hashline-edit/src/fs-write.ts` (~76 LOC) is the reference implementation; we port the same semantics adapted to our queue.

## Scope
In scope:
- New file `src/tools/hashline-edit/fs-write.ts` (~120 LOC) exporting:
  - `resolveWriteTarget(path: string)` returning `{ canonicalPath, isSymlink, hardLinkCount, mode }`.
  - `writeFileAtomically(targetPath, hardLinkCount, mode, content)` that:
    - If `hardLinkCount > 1`: `openSync(O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC)` + `writeSync` + `close` on the canonical path (in-place, preserves inode).
    - Else: write to `<dir>/.<basename>.tmp.<pid>.<rand>` in the SAME directory as target (to keep `rename` atomic on the same filesystem), `chmodSync` to `mode`, then `renameSync` over canonical target.
  - Catch `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`ENOSPC`/`EROFS` and rethrow as `Error` carrying `code` field so the caller can `formatError("E_WRITE_FAILED", ...)`.
- In `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts`, replace both `writeFileSync` call sites in `applyHashlineEdits` (current line `323` and the rename branch):
  - The normal write: resolve target once via `resolveWriteTarget`, call `writeFileAtomically`.
  - The rename case: resolve `rename` target (use `safeRealpath` from T2 — if rename target does not exist, use the literal path joined with dirname's realpath), write atomically there, then `unlinkSync(filePath)` (original).
  - BOM/CRLF restoration on `result` (existing logic above the write) is unchanged — atomic write operates on the final byte string and must preserve it across the rename path as well.
- Real-filesystem tests under `os.tmpdir()` in new `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/atomic-write.test.ts`.

Out of scope:
- `postEditVerify` integrity check (Phase 2 / T7).
- Windows-specific test coverage — skip atomic-write tests with `process.platform === "win32"` and a TODO; document in spec § 6 Risks.
- Cross-device rename handling (caller never points temp at a different filesystem because we always create temp in the target's directory).

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/fs-write.ts` (new).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — call sites in `applyHashlineEdits`; also wire `E_WRITE_FAILED` via `formatError` (T1).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/atomic-write.test.ts` (new) — 5 test cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T1 (errors): need `formatError` + `E_WRITE_FAILED` code to surface filesystem errors cleanly.
- T2 (canonical queue): reuses `safeRealpath` helper from T2 to resolve rename targets defensively.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Tests run on macOS + Linux. Windows is best-effort — `renameSync` semantics differ (replaces via `MoveFileExW`); document but do not gate CI on Windows correctness.
- Temp filename includes `pid` + random suffix to avoid collision with leftover from a previous interrupted run.
- `chmod` happens **before** `rename` so the new content has correct perms when it appears at the target name (atomicity property).
- BOM and CRLF round-trip logic already in `applyHashlineEdits` is unchanged — atomic write operates on the final `result` string.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Symlink-to-directory: `realpath` would return the directory; defensive check that the canonical path is a file before writing (otherwise return `E_WRITE_FAILED` with hint).
- Hard-link in-place truncation: if process is killed between `O_TRUNC` and final `writeSync`, file is empty. Document as known limitation; no `O_TMPFILE` fallback in this iteration.
- Permission preservation conflict: if the directory itself is unwritable, temp create fails — that is the expected EACCES path and tested.
- Avoid using `os.tmpdir()` directly as the temp location — always use `path.dirname(canonical)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 5 tests in `atomic-write.test.ts` pass:
  1. Symlink: writing through symlink updates the canonical file (assert via `readFileSync(canonical)`); symlink remains a symlink (`lstat`).

title: replace_text edit op (exact-unique substring)
description:
## Objective
Add a `replace_text` edit op that performs exact-unique substring replacement, giving the LLM a fallback when anchors are stale, without forcing a full re-read round-trip.

## Context
When the file changes between `read` and `edit`, every anchored edit fails with `E_HASH_MISMATCH` and the model must re-read. For local single-substitution intent (rename identifier, tweak literal), exact-unique text matching is faster and equally safe — `pi-hashline-edit` and `pi-hashline-readmap` both offer this. We add the operation but keep semantics strict: zero or multiple matches always fail with a typed error.

## Scope
In scope:
- Extend `EditSchema` union in `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` with `{ op: "replace_text", oldText: string, newText: string }`.
- In `applyHashlineEdits`, separate edits into `textEdits` (op === "replace_text") and the existing categories. Apply `textEdits` **first**, sequentially. After each text-edit:
  - Count exact occurrences of `oldText` in the current file content.
  - 0 → return `E_NO_MATCH` (no partial commit).
  - >1 → return `E_MULTI_MATCH`; include line numbers of the first 3 matches in the context block.
  - 1 → splice the replacement, recompute `fileLines` array for downstream edits.
- After all text-edits apply, re-validate every anchored edit's CID against the new snapshot — if CIDs no longer match (because the text-edit shifted lines), return `E_HASH_MISMATCH` with fresh anchors near the original line.
- Overlap detection extension: derive a `[startLine, endLine]` span for each `replace_text` match (start = line index containing first char of `oldText`, end = line index containing last char; multi-line `oldText` spans multiple lines). If any text-edit span intersects the `[pos.line, end.line]` range of an anchored `replace`, return `E_OVERLAP` with both edit indices.
- Update tool `description` listing the new op and stating its exact-unique semantics.

Out of scope:
- Fuzzy matching (whitespace-normalised, confusable-Unicode) — not in v1.
- `all: true` mode to replace all occurrences — not in v1; exact-unique only.
- Tree-sitter-aware structural matching (that is the `replace_symbol` Phase 3 idea).

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — schema extension; new branch in apply pipeline; overlap rules.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/replace-text.test.ts` (new) — 7 cases per spec § 4 T4.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T1 (errors): uses `formatError("E_NO_MATCH"|"E_MULTI_MATCH"|"E_OVERLAP"|"E_HASH_MISMATCH", ...)`.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `oldText` is matched after the file has been normalised through the existing BOM/CRLF logic — both sides are LF for matching. Document this in tool description so callers do not include `\r\n`.
- Empty `oldText` is rejected with `E_NO_MATCH` (defensive; otherwise would match between every char).
- Multi-line `oldText` (contains `\n`) is supported — splice over the corresponding line range.
- Ordering within `textEdits` is the array order from the caller; if a later text-edit's `oldText` only exists because of an earlier text-edit's `newText`, that is intentional and supported.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Counting occurrences naively with `split(oldText).length - 1` is fine for non-empty `oldText`; verify with overlapping-match edge (e.g. `oldText = "aa"` in `"aaaa"` → 2 non-overlapping matches; we treat as >1 → reject).
- Re-validating anchored edits after a text-edit is essential — without it, an anchored edit could land on the wrong line silently.
- Bottom-up sort for anchored edits is computed AFTER text-edits finalise the snapshot, so the existing sort logic still applies.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 7 cases in `replace-text.test.ts` (single match, zero match, multi match, mixed with anchored non-overlap, mixed overlap → `E_OVERLAP`, multi-line `oldText`, empty `oldText` → `E_NO_MATCH`).
- Existing tests untouched green.
- `bun run test`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` green.
close_reason: Implemented replace_text op: extended EditSchema with op='replace_text', oldText, newText. Text edits partition + apply BEFORE anchored edits, rebuilding fileLines snapshot after each. E_NO_MATCH (zero/empty), E_MULTI_MATCH (>1, with first 3 line numbers + hint), E_OVERLAP (text-span vs anchored range pre-mutation check). Added helpers countOccurrences/locateOccurrenceLines/detectTextAnchorOverlap. Updated tool description + prompt guideline. Added replace-text.test.ts with 8 cases (all 7 spec + chained sequential). 695/695 pass; lint/build/size green (138KB gzipped).

title: Diff preview + Updated anchors in edit response
description:
## Objective
After a successful edit, append two blocks to the response: `--- Updated anchors ---` (fresh `LINE#CID|content` for changed regions ± 3 context lines) and `--- Diff preview ---` (per-range `-` / `+` view with new CIDs on the `+` side and `OLD` placeholder on the `-` side). Also expose the structured diff in `details.diffData` so the TUI renderer (T9) can render an inline diff in expanded view.

## Context
Today the tool returns `File updated. N lines.` and nothing else. The model must re-`read` to perform any chained edit nearby — wasted tokens and a slow loop. Both `pi-hashline-edit` and `pi-hashline-readmap` surface updated anchors and/or diffs in the response so a follow-up edit can run without a re-read. We do not need LCS because the input edits already deterministically describe which line ranges changed.

## Scope
In scope:
- New file `src/tools/hashline-edit/diff-preview.ts` exporting:
  - `computeChangedRanges(edits, oldLineCount): Array<{ oldStart, oldEnd, newStart, newEnd }>` — derived from the edit array bottom-up, tracking index shifts deterministically. No LCS.
  - `renderUpdatedAnchors(newLines, ranges, contextRadius = 3): string` — emits `LINE#CID|content` for each range with context lines on each side, blank line between ranges.
  - `renderDiffPreview(oldLines, newLines, ranges): string` — per range, emits removed lines as `- <lineNo>| <old content>` and added lines as `+ <lineNo>#<CID>| <new content>`. The `-` side intentionally OMITS a CID (because the line no longer exists) and uses `<lineNo>|` (no `#`); this format does NOT match the strict-patch regex `/^\d+#[A-Z]{2}\|/` from T1, so even if the model copies a diff line into a follow-up `lines` payload it will not collide. The `+` side uses the standard `LINE#CID|` form so the model can lift the new anchor directly.
  - Per-line diff prefix: `- ` (minus + space) for removals, `+ ` (plus + space) for additions, both followed by the formatted line as above.
  - Cap `MAX_DIFF_LINES = 50`; overflow → middle-cut with marker `[… N lines elided …]`.
- In `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts`:
  - Snapshot `oldLines = [...fileLines]` BEFORE applying edits.
  - After successful write, compute ranges, render both blocks, append to success message.
  - Populate `details.diffData = { oldLineSlices, newLineSlices, ranges }` (only the slices needed by the renderer, not full files) so T9 can consume without re-deriving.
- New test `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/diff-preview.test.ts` covering 7 cases per spec § 4 T5.

Out of scope:
- TUI rendering of the diff (T9, Phase 2).
- Difftastic semantic classification.
- Re-reading the file after write to verify (T7, Phase 2).

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/diff-preview.ts` (new).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — snapshot pre-apply; append rendered blocks; populate `details.diffData`.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/diff-preview.test.ts` (new).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- None hard; soft-couples with T3 (atomic write) for write-then-render ordering, but compute happens in-memory and is independent of write path. Sequence after T1-T4 ideally so error taxonomy and `replace_text` are integrated — but no schema or executor conflict.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The `details.diffData` schema is internal; T9 owns its render. Keep it simple: `Array<{ oldStart, oldEnd, oldLines: string[], newStart, newEnd, newLines: string[] }>`.
- `MAX_DIFF_LINES = 50` is total across all ranges combined; tested explicitly.
- For pure append (no `-` lines) or pure delete (no `+` lines), the renderer emits only the applicable side; no empty `±` markers.
- The Updated anchors block re-runs `computeCID` from `src/utils/cid.ts` on the post-write `fileLines` — keep that single source of truth.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Range merging: if two close edits produce overlapping context windows, merge ranges before render to avoid duplicate lines. Implement a final pass that merges adjacent ranges (newStart_n ≤ newEnd_{n-1}+2*radius).
- Bottom-up edit ordering: `computeChangedRanges` must walk edits in the same bottom-up order as `applyHashlineEdits` to keep line-number arithmetic consistent.
- Response size: even with cap, ensure the full message + diff stays under `compactHashlineError`'s threshold so success path is not accidentally trimmed (compactor currently only fires for errors — confirm before relying).

## Acceptance Criteria
- 7 cases in `diff-preview.test.ts` (single-line replace; range 5→3 replace; pure append; pure delete via `lines: null`; multiple non-overlapping edits; overflow with middle-cut; the `- <lineNo>| ...` removed-line format does NOT match `/^\d+#[A-Z]{2}\|/` even when copied verbatim).
- A success response in a representative test demonstrates both blocks present and well-formed.
- `bun run test`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` green.
close_reason: Implemented diff-preview.ts (~165 LOC): computeChangedRanges via deterministic prefix/suffix trim (no LCS); renderUpdatedAnchors (LINE#CID|content +/-3 context); renderDiffPreview ('- <ln>| ...' WITHOUT '#' to avoid strict-patch regex collision, '+ <ln>#<CID>| ...' for added); MAX_DIFF_LINES=50 middle-cut elision. index.ts: snapshot oldLines pre-mutation; buildSuccessResult appends preview blocks; details.diffData populated for T9. Added diff-preview.test.ts with 12 cases (5 computeChangedRanges + 4 renderDiffPreview incl. critical strict-patch-regex non-match + 1 renderUpdatedAnchors + 2 E2E). v1 trade-off: multiple disjoint edits collapse into one coarse range (documented in spec § Risks). 707/707 pass; lint/build/size green (140KB gzipped).

title: postEditVerify opt-in flag with rollback
description:
## Objective
Add an opt-in `postEditVerify: boolean` top-level parameter to `hashline_edit`. When set, after a successful atomic write, read the file back from disk, re-apply BOM/CRLF restoration logic, and compare byte-for-byte against the intended `result` string. On mismatch, attempt rollback and return `E_VERIFY_FAILED`.

## Context
Atomic write (T3) protects against truncation, but not against subtle corruption from encoding edge cases, filesystem-level mangling (e.g. CRLF translation on misconfigured Windows), or write-success-but-content-different bugs. `pi-hashline-readmap` ships this as a per-call flag (default off, fast path is preserved).

## Scope
In scope:
- New file `src/tools/hashline-edit/post-verify.ts` exporting `verifyPersistedContent(canonicalPath, intendedResult, { hasBOM, hasCRLF }): { ok: true } | { ok: false; diffContext: string }`.
- Extend `HashlineEditSchema` in `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` with optional `postEditVerify?: boolean` (default `false`).
- In `applyHashlineEdits`, after `writeFileAtomically` succeeds, when flag is set, call `verifyPersistedContent`. On `ok: false`:
  - Attempt rollback: write `oldContent` (pre-write snapshot already in memory) back via `writeFileAtomically`.
  - Return `formatError("E_VERIFY_FAILED", message, diffContext)` regardless of rollback outcome. If rollback failed, append a second-line warning: "Rollback failed; file may be partially corrupted, inspect manually."
- New test `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/post-verify.test.ts` covering: happy path (verify passes), simulated mismatch (mock `readFileSync` after write), rollback success path, rollback fail path (mock both writes).

Out of scope:
- Default-on behaviour (always off; users opt in per call).
- Verifying against a different intended representation (e.g. hash-based) — direct string comparison is sufficient and lets us produce a useful diff context.
- Persistent state across calls.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/post-verify.ts` (new).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — schema; verify branch after write.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/post-verify.test.ts` (new).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T3 (atomic write): rollback uses `writeFileAtomically` and the canonical-path resolution.
- T1 (errors): `E_VERIFY_FAILED` code wired here.
- Phase 1 closure (T6) is preferred but not strictly required — only schema concern is the new optional field which does not break existing payloads.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Intended `result` string is what `applyHashlineEdits` produces post BOM/CRLF restoration, so the comparison is against the same bytes that should appear on disk.
- Pre-write snapshot for rollback is the in-scope `rawContent` variable (already captured at `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts:185` before BOM/CRLF normalisation). Rollback writes `rawContent` back via `writeFileAtomically` to the canonical path — this restores the original bytes including any BOM/CRLF.
- Tests use `node:test`'s built-in `mock.method(fs, "readFileSync", ...)` (available since Node ≥20.6, which matches the project's `engines.node` floor). No DI refactor required.
- `diffContext` is the first ~200 chars around where bytes diverge, with line + column locators. Cap to keep response compact.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Rollback uses the SAME atomic write path — if filesystem is broken (ENOSPC, EROFS), rollback also fails. Honest reporting in the error message is mandatory; do not silently swallow.
- Performance: extra read-back doubles syscall cost per edit. Flag MUST default off and be documented as opt-in.
- Race: another process could mutate the file between write and verify. Out of scope to mitigate — document.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 4 tests pass in `post-verify.test.ts`.
- Flag absent / `false` keeps existing fast path (no extra read).
- Existing tests untouched green.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` green.
close_reason: Implemented postEditVerify: new post-verify.ts (~85 LOC) with verifyPersistedContent + injectable readFn seam (default readFileSync). Extended HashlineEditSchema with optional postEditVerify boolean. Extended ApplyHashlineEditsOptions with __verifyReadFn/__rollbackWriteFn test hooks (ESM-immutable fs precluded mock.method). On mismatch: rollback via writeFileAtomically using pre-edit rawContent + BOM restoration; rollback-failure branch surfaces 'partially corrupted' warning. Added post-verify.test.ts (7 cases): 3 pure verifyPersistedContent + 4 integration (happy, flag-absent, mismatch+rollback-restores, mismatch+rollback-fails). 714/714 pass; lint/build/size green (143KB gzipped).

title: Edit variant aliases (insert_after / insert_before / replace_range)
description:
## Objective
Add three op aliases to `hashline_edit`'s schema (`insert_after`, `insert_before`, `replace_range`) that normalise to the existing canonical ops (`append` with `pos`, `prepend` with `pos`, `replace` with `end`) so the LLM can express intent more clearly without changing behaviour.

## Context
The current op vocabulary (`replace` / `append` / `prepend`) is ambiguous: `append` without `pos` means EOF; with `pos` means "after this anchor"; `prepend` mirrors. Readmap-style names (`insert_after`, `insert_before`, `replace_range`) communicate intent better and reduce LLM ambiguity. Adding aliases — not renaming — keeps 100% backward compatibility.

## Scope
In scope:
- Extend `EditSchema` op union in `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` with literals `"insert_after"`, `"insert_before"`, `"replace_range"`.
- Add `normalizeEdit(edit): Edit` helper that maps:
  - `insert_after` → `append` (require `pos`; reject with `E_BAD_REF` if missing — these aliases are anchored-only by design).
  - `insert_before` → `prepend` (same `pos` requirement).
  - `replace_range` → `replace` (require both `pos` and `end`).
- Apply `normalizeEdit` at the top of `applyHashlineEdits` so the rest of the executor stays unchanged.
- Update tool `description` to list all 6 op names with a one-line note: "`insert_after`/`insert_before`/`replace_range` are clearer aliases for `append`/`prepend`/`replace`."

Out of scope:
- Deprecating the original op names.
- Behaviour differences between aliases and canonical ops — they are exact behavioural aliases after `pos`/`end` requirement validation.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — schema; new `normalizeEdit`; tool description.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/hashline-edit.test.ts` — 3 new alias tests; assert existing op tests unchanged.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T1 (errors): missing `pos`/`end` on alias → `formatError("E_BAD_REF", ...)`.
- Phase 1 closure (T6) preferred so the error path is consistent.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Aliases are strictly stricter than originals (`pos` mandatory on the two insert aliases). This is the intended UX win — if a caller wanted EOF, they should still use `append` without `pos`.
- No JSON schema title/description changes that would alter typebox type signatures consumers rely on.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Make sure the union type discriminator still narrows correctly in TypeScript after adding three new literals — exhaustiveness checks may need updating in `applyHashlineEdits`'s switch (currently if/else on `op`).
- Tests for `prepend` without `pos` (BOF insert) must keep passing — aliases must not change canonical behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 3 new alias tests (one per alias, including `pos`-missing rejection) pass.
- Existing tests for `append`/`prepend`/`replace` all green.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` green.
close_reason: Implemented 3 alias ops: insert_after→append+pos, insert_before→prepend+pos, replace_range→replace+pos+end. EditSchema literals extended; normalizeEdit() runs at top of applyHashlineEdits so rest of executor sees only canonical ops. Missing pos/end on aliases → [E_BAD_REF] (E_BAD_REF). Tool description updated with alias note. 6 new tests in hashline-edit.test.ts (3 happy + 3 missing-anchor). 720/720 pass; lint/build/size green (144KB gzipped).

title: Inline TUI diff in expanded view
description:
## Objective
Replace `hashline_edit`'s generic `buildStatsRenderResult` renderer with a custom `renderResult` that reuses the collapsed view (`✓ <summary>`) and, in expanded view (Ctrl+O), renders the diff inline using text-mode markers (`▌+ ` / `▌- ` / `▌  `) in addition to colour.

## Context
T5 already populates `details.diffData` with the changed slices. The user currently has to open the file in another tool to see what changed. An inline diff matches the project's expanded-view convention (see `src/sub-agents/render.ts`) and uses text gutter markers so the diff is visible in plain-text transcripts and screen readers, not just in colour terminals.

## Scope
In scope:
- New file `src/tools/hashline-edit/result-renderer.ts` (~150 LOC) exporting `renderHashlineEditResult(result, options, theme, context)`:
  - Collapsed: `✓ <summary>` (same as today via `buildStatsRenderResult` baseline).
  - Expanded: header (`✓ <summary>`) + blank line + diff block.
  - Diff block, per range from `details.diffData`:
    - `▌- <content>` in `theme.fg("error", ...)` for each removed line.
    - `▌+ <content>` in `theme.fg("success", ...)` for each added line.
    - Optional context lines as `▌  <content>` in `theme.fg("muted", ...)` (only if `diffData` includes context — keep simple in v1, may be empty).
  - Width clamp: `clampLinesToWidth` is NOT exported from `src/sub-agents/format.ts` (verified). Duplicate a small ~10-line helper in `result-renderer.ts`: takes `(line: string, width: number) → string`, truncates to `width-1` chars + `…` when exceeded. No wrap, no ANSI awareness in v1.
  - Failure path unchanged — keep `buildHashlineErrorResult` for errors.
- Wire the new renderer into the tool registration in `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` (replace `renderResult: buildStatsRenderResult({ partial: "Editing..." })` with the new function while preserving the `partial: "Editing..."` text exactly — currently produced by the `buildStatsRenderResult` factory's partial-state branch; the new renderer must check `result === undefined` (or the equivalent partial signal in the render `context`) and emit `"Editing..."` muted so live UX is unchanged).
- New test `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/result-renderer.test.ts` using the same per-slot stub theme pattern as `src/sub-agents/__tests__/render.test.ts` so assertions can verify colour tokens by name (`error`, `success`, `muted`) without depending on actual ANSI codes.

Out of scope:
- Changing the success message string (T5 already shaped the response text).
- Difftastic or syntax-highlighted rendering.
- Animation / spinner.

## Components Touched
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/result-renderer.ts` (new).
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/index.ts` — swap `renderResult` wiring.
- `src/tools/hashline-edit/__tests__/result-renderer.test.ts` (new).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T5 (diff preview): consumes `details.diffData` schema produced by T5.
- Phase 1 closure (T6) preferred but not blocking — T5's data shape is the only contract needed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `theme.fg("success" | "error" | "muted", ...)` tokens are valid in the pi-tui theme — verify via existing usage in `src/sub-agents/render.ts` before authoring.
- Inline diff with no diff data (e.g. delete-only or rename-only tool result where no edits applied) must render gracefully — collapsed-only is fine.
- Width: respect `options.width` if provided; otherwise long lines truncate, do not wrap (consistent with sub-agent expanded panel).

## Risks / Gotchas
- Theme initialisation: `keyHint()` and similar helpers can throw in tests/boot — see post-mortem of `subagent-ui-polish.md` (T3 rollback). Do not invoke theme helpers at module-load; only inside the render closure.
- `buildStatsRenderResult` factory currently encapsulates the partial-state spinner; verify the partial-state behaviour is preserved or re-implement it in the new renderer.
- Large diff (50 lines after T5's cap) should not crash on narrow terminals — clamp per line.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Implement bundled Kiro provider Phase 1 MVP
description:
## Objective
Deliver the Phase 1 MVP for a config-gated bundled Kiro provider in Blackbytes.

## Context
This feature replaces reliance on an external Kiro provider for the Kiro-specific surfaces Blackbytes needs to own: provider aliases, credential compatibility, provider-local retry, redaction, tests, docs, and rollback.

## Scope
In scope:
- Provider config/registration, credential readers/resolution, Kiro models/stream/retry, status redaction, docs, and final verification.
Out of scope:
- Automatic account rotation, a GUI/command account manager, writing active Kiro IDE or kiro-cli token files as normal multi-account flow, global Pi retry changes, new runtime dependencies, or replacing other model providers.

## Components Touched
- src/config/schema.ts and config tests.
- New src/providers/kiro/* provider modules and tests.
- src/handlers/index.ts session_start registration.
- src/commands/blackbytes-status.ts and tests.
- README.md, AGENTS.md, and optional CHANGELOG.md.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Execute child beads according to their dependency edges.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Default provider id is `kirob` (`Kirob` user-facing label).
- Phase 1 preserves upstream-compatible Pi OAuth hooks.
- No new runtime dependency unless a follow-up ADR/spec is created.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Kiro sends no Retry-After on observed throttles; retry must classify by body and generate long backoff locally.
- True separate-account isolation only exists for per-alias Pi OAuth or distinct API keys, not shared kiro-cli/IDE sources.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- All child beads are complete.
- `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run build && bun run test` and `bun run check:size` pass or any failure is documented honestly.

## Success Criteria
- `blackbytes.kiro.enabled=true` registers default alias `kirob` from existing IDE/CLI credentials.
- Two configured accounts register two independent provider aliases in one session.
- Kiro transient 429 retry is provider-local, abortable, body-classified, uses long generated backoff, swallows intermediate 429s, and does not retry monthly quota bodies.
- Capacity retry remains separate from 429 retry.
- `/blackbytes-status`, README, AGENTS, tests, rollback docs, and package-size verification are complete.

description:

- Detect `INSUFFICIENT_MODEL_CAPACITY` as a separate capacity retry pattern.
- Honor Retry-After only as best-effort hint if present; do not depend on it.

title: Implement chain executor module with timeout budget and stop-on-failure
description:
## Objective
Create src/sub-agents/chain.ts with the sequential chain executor. Core function: executeChain(options: ChainOptions): Promise<ChainResult>. Implements sequential execution, timeout budget allocation, stop-on-failure (default), and continue-on-failure modes.

## Context
The chain executor runs 2-5 existing sub-agents in sequence, passing each step output to the next. It reuses the existing delegate infrastructure (register.ts, runner.ts, fallback.ts) rather than creating a new spawn mechanism.

## Scope
In scope:
- Define ChainStep interface: { agent: string, question: string, context?: string, timeoutMs?: number }
- Define ChainOptions interface: { steps: ChainStep[], totalTimeoutMs: number, continueOnFailure?: boolean }
- Define ChainStepResult interface: { agent: string, success: boolean, content: string, durationMs: number, failureKind?: DelegateFailureKind }
- Define ChainResult interface: { success: boolean, steps: ChainStepResult[], totalDurationMs: number, stoppedEarly: boolean }
- Implement allocateTimeoutBudget(): split totalTimeoutMs across remaining steps
- Implement executeChain(): iterate steps sequentially, compose context with prior output, enforce timeout budget
- Stop on first failure by default; continueOnFailure overrides
- Reject chains with 0 or >5 steps
- Reject disabled/unknown agent names before execution starts
- Import and use runNestedPi() from runner.ts for each step execution
- Import DelegateFailureKind from types.ts for failure classification

Out of scope:
- Public tool registration (decision deferred to Phase 3, Q-001)
- YAML chain DSL
- Fanout, async polling, inter-agent chat
- Fallback model logic (chain steps use single model, no fallback)

## Components Touched
- src/sub-agents/chain.ts — new file with executeChain(), allocateTimeoutBudget(), and types
- src/sub-agents/types.ts — export chain types (ChainStep, ChainOptions, ChainStepResult, ChainResult)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- None (pure module, can be developed in parallel with REQ-004)

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Each step uses runNestedPi() directly (not executeWithFallback — chain does not need fallback logic)
- delegate_* tools never leak into chain step sessions (existing allowlist enforcement in runNestedPi handles this)
- Total timeout is hard cap; allocateTimeoutBudget divides remaining time evenly across remaining steps
- Chain is internal-only in Phase 2 (no public delegate_chain tool)
- Chain steps must use agents that are registered and enabled (validate before execution)

## Risks / Gotchas
- Must not create recursive delegation (chain steps must not have delegate_* tools — runNestedPi enforces this)
- Timeout budget exhaustion: if a step uses its full allocation, remaining steps may get very small slices
- Step output passed as context to next step could grow large; rely on existing MAX_RETURN_CHARS bounding
- Chain executor must validate agent names against registered agents before starting execution

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unit tests in src/sub-agents/__tests__/chain.test.ts covering: sequential execution order, previous-output propagation, stop-on-failure, continue-on-failure, disabled agent rejection, total timeout budget exhaustion, per-step timeout, empty chain rejection, single-step chain, >5 step rejection
- All tests pass with node:test and node:assert/strict
- Module exports all public functions and types
- bun test passes

## Acceptance Criteria
- `src/sub-agents/chain.ts` exports `executeChain()` and `allocateTimeoutBudget()` and implements the `ChainStep`, `ChainOptions`, `ChainStepResult`, and `ChainResult` contract exported from `types.ts`.
- Chains with 0 steps or more than 5 steps are rejected before any nested run starts; unknown or disabled agent names are also rejected up front.
- Steps execute strictly sequentially, pass prior output under a clear `## Previous step output` heading, enforce total/per-step timeout budgets, and stop on first failure unless `continueOnFailure` is true.
- Chain execution reuses `runNestedPi()` and does not introduce public tool registration, recursive delegation, fallback-model orchestration, fanout, async polling, or YAML chain DSL.
- Unit tests cover sequential order, previous-output propagation, stop/continue-on-failure, disabled/unknown agent rejection, timeout budget exhaustion, per-step timeout, empty/single/>5 step cases, and exports.
- `bun test` passes.

description:
Prompt System Hardening Phase 1 MVP tracks the implementation of docs/specs/prompt-system-hardening.md.

Scope:
- Oracle long-context and high-risk self-check guardrails.
- Oracle/General GPT prompt variants selected only from a configured nested model.
- General prompt static tool-list removal.
- Typed routing metadata and metadata-driven Bytes overlay/status rendering.
- Delegate description tightening and verification.

Out of scope: YAML system_prompt_by_family, fallback per-attempt prompt switching, new tools/agents, Reviewer bash access, and status UI redesign beyond one new section.

Implementation note:
- This is a tracking parent, not the implementation bead. Implement T-001..T-008, then close this root after T-008 records integrated verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- T-001..T-008 are closed.
- `bun run lint && bun run build && bun run test` passes.
- `/blackbytes-status` shows Sub-Agent Routing.

title: T-001 Add declaration and YAML routing scaffolding
description:
## Objective
Add typed declaration and runtime metadata scaffolding for sub-agent routing and per-family prompt bodies, plus optional YAML routing support.

## Context
Prompt System Hardening needs routing metadata to be available to overlay/status consumers without parsing descriptions, and needs declarations to carry optional family-specific prompt bodies. This bead provides the type/schema foundation before prompt text or consumer behavior changes.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `SubAgentRoutingMetadata`, `systemPromptByFamily?`, and `routing?` to `SubAgentDeclaration`.
- Extend `SubAgentMeta` and `declarationToMeta()` so routing survives runtime registration.
- Extend YAML loader with optional `routing:` only.
- Add validation caps for routing fields.
Out of scope:
- YAML `system_prompt_by_family` support.
- Prompt text changes.
- Overlay/status routing rendering.

## Type Shapes

`SubAgentRoutingMetadata` (new type in `declaration.ts`):
```ts
export interface SubAgentRoutingMetadata {
  category: "exploration" | "reasoning" | "research" | "implementation" | "review";
  cost: "low" | "medium" | "high";
  useWhen: string[];     // max 6 items, each ≤ 60 chars
  avoidWhen: string[];   // max 6 items, each ≤ 60 chars
  keyTrigger?: string;   // optional one-line trigger summary
}
```

`systemPromptByFamily` (new optional field on `SubAgentDeclaration`):
```ts
systemPromptByFamily?: Partial<Record<ModelFamily, string>>;
```
Reuse `ModelFamily` from `src/shared/model-capability.ts`.

## Components Touched
- `src/sub-agents/declaration.ts` — declaration types and meta conversion.
- `src/config/resource-metadata.ts` — `SubAgentMeta` routing field.
- `src/sub-agents/loader.ts` — optional YAML routing schema and conversion.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/loader.test.ts` — YAML routing validation/round-trip coverage.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/snapshot.test.ts` or adjacent tests — declaration/meta copy coverage.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- No prerequisite bead.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- All new fields are optional for backward compatibility.
- YAML agents without `routing` must continue loading unchanged.
- Invalid YAML routing must skip the offending file with diagnostics rather than crash at runtime.
- `useWhen` and `avoidWhen` are capped at 6 short entries each (≤ 60 chars per item).
- `category` must be one of the five enum values; any other value is invalid.
- Canonical routing enum values for this implementation are the values in the Type Shapes section above: categories `exploration | reasoning | research | implementation | review`, and costs `low | medium | high`. Do not use older draft names such as `advisor`, `specialist`, `executor`, `utility`, `free`, `cheap`, or `expensive` if encountered in stale spec text.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Do not introduce a second model-family type here; prompt-family behavior belongs in T-002 and must reuse `src/shared/model-capability.ts`.
- Avoid importing builtin declarations into UI/status code; routing should travel through metadata.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Typecheck passes for builtin and YAML declarations.
- Loader round-trip tests prove YAML `routing` is accepted and copied.
- Loader diagnostics tests prove invalid routing values are skipped safely.
- Declaration/meta tests prove `routing` is copied by `declarationToMeta()`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typecheck passes for builtin and YAML declarations with the new optional fields.
- `SubAgentRoutingMetadata` type matches the specified shape (5 enum categories, cost enum, capped arrays).
- `systemPromptByFamily` typed as `Partial<Record<ModelFamily, string>>` reusing existing `ModelFamily`.
- Loader round-trip tests prove YAML `routing` is accepted and copied.
- Loader diagnostics tests prove invalid routing values are skipped safely.
- Declaration/meta tests prove `routing` is copied by `declarationToMeta()`.
- YAML agents without `routing` still load unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented and verified

title: T-002 Resolve sub-agent prompt bodies from configured nested model
description:
## Objective
Resolve each sub-agent prompt body from the configured nested model, selecting family-specific variants only when `snapshot.model` is explicitly configured.

## Context
Oracle and General need GPT-optimized prompt bodies, but parent/host model family must not leak into nested sub-agent prompt selection. This bead changes the prompt builder and registrar wiring so the active per-agent snapshot drives prompt-body selection.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `resolveSystemPromptBody(decl, modelId?)` in the existing `src/sub-agents/prompt-builder.ts` (which already exports `buildSystemPrompt()`).
- Use `classifyModel()` from `src/shared/model-capability.ts`; do not duplicate `ModelFamily`.
- Wire the resolved body into `buildSystemPrompt({ basePrompt, ... })` from `registerSubAgent()` so the snapshot-selected body becomes the base prompt.
- Preserve existing `promptMode` handling and append-mode fail-loud behavior.
Out of scope:
- Adding actual Oracle/General GPT prompt text.
- Changing fallback runner semantics or per-attempt prompt switching.

## Current Wiring in register.ts
`registerSubAgent()` already resolves the per-agent snapshot via `getAgentSnapshotFor(declaration.name)` **before** calling `buildSystemPrompt({ basePrompt: declaration.systemPrompt, ... })`. Today `basePrompt` is hardcoded to `declaration.systemPrompt`. The change needed: replace that argument with `resolveSystemPromptBody(declaration, snapshot?.model)` so the resolved model drives family classification. If `snapshot?.model` is undefined, use the default `systemPrompt`; never fall through to the parent's cached model family.

## Components Touched
- `src/sub-agents/prompt-builder.ts` — add prompt body resolver (file exists; extends current module).
- `src/sub-agents/register.ts` — pass resolved body as `basePrompt` (no ordering change needed; snapshot is already looked up first).
- `src/shared/model-capability.ts` — reused classifier only, no new family type.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/prompt-builder.test.ts` — resolver behavior.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/delegates.test.ts` — captured `--system-prompt` behavior.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T-001 must be complete because this uses the new `systemPromptByFamily?` declaration field.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- No configured nested model means default `systemPrompt`, even if the parent cached family is GPT.
- Configured GPT-family nested model uses `systemPromptByFamily.gpt` when present.
- Non-GPT models and missing family variants fall back to default `systemPrompt`.
- `fallbackModels` do not affect prompt-body selection in this iteration.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Passing `declaration.systemPrompt` (instead of the resolved body) to `buildSystemPrompt` silently selects the wrong body.
- Using `resolvePromptModelFamily()` would incorrectly consult parent/cached family; use `classifyModel(snapshot.model)` only when `snapshot?.model` exists.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Prompt-builder tests cover default, GPT variant, missing variant fallback, non-GPT fallback, and append-mode error behavior.
- Register-level tests capture nested `--system-prompt` and prove default vs GPT selection.
- A regression test proves parent cached GPT family does not change prompt body when nested model is unset.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Prompt-builder tests cover default, GPT variant, missing variant fallback, non-GPT fallback, and append-mode error behavior.
- Register-level tests capture nested `--system-prompt` and prove default vs GPT selection.
- A regression test proves parent cached GPT family does not change prompt body when nested model is unset.
close_reason: Implemented and verified

title: T-003 Harden Oracle prompt and add Oracle GPT variant
description:
## Objective
Harden the Oracle default prompt with long-context and high-risk self-check guardrails, and add the Oracle GPT prompt variant.

## Context
Oracle handles hard architecture/debugging/security/performance reasoning. It needs stronger grounding behavior for large contexts and a GPT-friendly output shape when a GPT nested model is explicitly configured.

## Scope
In scope:
- Append `## Long-Context Handling` and `## High-Risk Self-Check` after `## Scope Discipline` in `ORACLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`.
- Add `ORACLE_GPT_PROMPT` in `src/sub-agents/oracle.ts`.
- Wire `systemPromptByFamily.gpt` on `oracleDeclaration`.
Out of scope:
- Changing Oracle allowed tools, mutability, timeout, or reasoning defaults.
- Adding GPT variants for Explore, Librarian, or Reviewer.

## Prompt Body Requirements
- Default Oracle prompt: append `## Long-Context Handling` and `## High-Risk Self-Check` immediately after `## Scope Discipline` and before output-style guidance; keep the default-prompt growth to roughly ≤14 lines.
- Oracle GPT prompt: include an explicit opener blacklist, keep effort tags `Quick`, `Short`, `Medium`, and `Large`, keep the self-contained final-message requirement, and use prose-first answers for simple questions instead of forcing the full structured template.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Keep the self-contained final message requirement.
- Keep effort tags: Quick, Short, Medium, Large.
- Keep uncertainty/no-fabrication rules, read-only constraints, and language matching.
- GPT variant should be prose-first and avoid forcing the 6-point template for trivial questions.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Do not copy oc-blackbytes wording verbatim; keep pi's Markdown-heading style and file-reference convention.
- Do not bloat the default prompt more than the planned ≤14 added lines.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Snapshot/prompt tests prove both new default sections exist in the specified location.
- Tests prove `sub_agents.oracle.model = "gpt-*"` sends the GPT body to nested Pi.
- Default Oracle users still receive the default prompt body unless a nested GPT model is configured.
## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests prove `sub_agents.oracle.model = "gpt-*"` sends the GPT body to nested Pi.
- Default Oracle users still receive the default prompt body unless a nested GPT model is configured.

title: T-004 Clean up General prompt and add General GPT variant
description:
## Objective
Remove General's duplicated static tool list and add the General GPT prompt variant.

## Context
General already receives an authoritative safety/context overlay with the finalized allowed tools. The static prompt list can drift and currently duplicates tool names that should be sourced from runtime policy.

## Scope
In scope:
- Replace General's `## Tool Access` list with the overlay-deferring paragraph (see content below).
- Remove the now-unused `TOOL_NAMES` import from `src/sub-agents/general.ts`.
- Add `GENERAL_GPT_PROMPT` and wire `systemPromptByFamily.gpt`.
Out of scope:
- Changing General allowed-tool resolution, mutability, or safety overlay content.
- Adding YAML per-family prompt support.

## Replacement Paragraph for `## Tool Access`
Replace the 8-bullet interpolated tool list that currently uses `TOOL_NAMES.*` constants with this overlay-deferring text:

```md
## Tool Access

The host prepends a safety/context overlay containing the **finalized allowed
tool list** for this invocation along with working directory, repository
conventions from `AGENTS.md`, and verification commands. Treat that overlay as
the authoritative source of truth for what is callable and how to verify work —
do not attempt tools that are not listed there.
```

The safety overlay from `src/sub-agents/general-safety-overlay.ts` already carries the real allowed tool list at runtime. The old phrase `Depending on session configuration` belongs to the removed static-list block and should not remain in `generalDeclaration.systemPrompt`.

## Components Touched
- `src/sub-agents/general.ts` — prompt body and imports.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/general.test.ts` — static-list regression tests.
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/delegates.test.ts` — configured GPT prompt capture.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T-002 must be complete so `systemPromptByFamily.gpt` is resolved at runtime.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Preserve Plan-Sanity Check behavior.
- Preserve no-follow-up, no scope expansion, no recursive agent, verification, and language-matching constraints.
- The runtime overlay remains the authoritative source for the allowed tool list and repo verification commands.

## Risks / Gotchas
- A test for literal `TOOL_NAMES.*` inside `generalDeclaration.systemPrompt` is ineffective because interpolation removes the literal token. Instead, test that the source file no longer imports `TOOL_NAMES` and that the prompt text does not contain the old bullet markers (e.g., no `— find files by pattern`, `— AST-aware search`).
- Do not accidentally remove General's strict gating from the tool description.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- General prompt text contains the overlay-deferring paragraph (e.g., includes "finalized allowed tool list") and does not contain `Depending on session configuration` or the old static tool-list bullets.
- Source-level or text test proves `src/sub-agents/general.ts` no longer imports `TOOL_NAMES`.
- Tests prove `sub_agents.general.model = "gpt-*"` sends the GPT body to nested Pi.

## Acceptance Criteria
- General prompt text contains the overlay-deferring paragraph and does not contain old static tool-list bullets.
- `src/sub-agents/general.ts` no longer imports `TOOL_NAMES`.
- Tests prove `sub_agents.general.model = "gpt-*"` sends the GPT body to nested Pi.

title: T-005 Populate builtin routing metadata and routing summary helper
description:
## Objective
Populate builtin sub-agent routing metadata and provide a deterministic routing summary helper.

## Context
Routing intent should be a typed source of truth instead of duplicated across delegate descriptions and hardcoded overlay strings. This bead provides the metadata and helper that consumers use later.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `routing` metadata to Explore, Oracle, Librarian, General, and Reviewer declarations.
- Add `src/sub-agents/routing.ts` with `buildRoutingSummary(metas, enabledSubAgents)`.
- Cover builtin completeness, deterministic ordering, enabled filtering, and YAML placeholder behavior.
Out of scope:
- Rendering routing in the Bytes overlay or status command.
- Shortening tool descriptions.

## Routing Metadata Style Guide
Derive routing values from each builtin's existing delegate description. Keep entries concise:
- `useWhen` / `avoidWhen`: ≤ 6 items each, ≤ 60 chars per item.
- `keyTrigger`: one-line summary of when to delegate.

Example for Oracle (calibrates the expected granularity):
```ts
routing: {
  category: "reasoning",
  cost: "high",
  useWhen: [
    "Hard architecture or debugging decisions",
    "Security or performance trade-off analysis",
    "After 2 failed attempts at solving a problem",
  ],
  avoidWhen: [
    "Simple questions answerable from local code",
    "Tasks that need file writes or bash execution",
  ],
  keyTrigger: "Deep analytical reasoning on hard problems",
}
```

Expected categories:
- explore → `"exploration"`, cost `"medium"`
- oracle → `"reasoning"`, cost `"high"`
- librarian → `"research"`, cost `"high"`
- general → `"implementation"`, cost `"high"`
- reviewer → `"review"`, cost `"medium"`

## Components Touched
- `src/sub-agents/explore.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/oracle.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/librarian.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/general.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/reviewer.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/routing.ts` (new file)
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/routing.test.ts` (new file)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T-001 must be complete because routing metadata fields must exist on declarations and metadata.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Routing metadata has `category`, `cost`, `useWhen`, `avoidWhen`, and optional `keyTrigger`.
- YAML agents without routing must produce a placeholder entry (e.g., `"—"`) for status output, not an error.
- `buildRoutingSummary()` consumes runtime `SubAgentMeta[]` (from the metadata registry), not builtin declarations directly.
- Use registration/input order for deterministic summaries unless an existing caller already documents a different stable ordering; tests must lock the chosen order so overlay and status stay consistent.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Keep routing descriptions concise; do not re-create the full verbose delegate descriptions in metadata.
- Ensure the helper consumes runtime `SubAgentMeta` so consumers do not import builtin declarations directly.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Tests prove all 5 builtins have complete routing metadata.
- Tests prove disabled agents are filtered from summaries.
- Tests prove output ordering is stable (deterministic, e.g., alphabetical or registration order).
- Tests prove YAML/no-routing placeholder behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 5 builtins have complete routing metadata matching the style guide.
- Disabled agents are filtered from summaries.
- Output ordering is stable and deterministic.
- YAML agents without routing produce placeholder output.
close_reason: Implemented and verified

title: T-007 Tighten delegate tool descriptions without losing gates
description:
## Objective
Shorten delegate tool descriptions by removing duplicated positive routing prose while preserving strict delegation gates and cost signals.

## Context
Once routing metadata drives the Bytes overlay, delegate descriptions no longer need to repeat positive `useWhen` lists. The descriptions must still protect against costly or incorrect delegation, especially for Librarian and General.

## Scope
In scope:
- Shorten descriptions in all 5 builtin sub-agent declarations.
- Preserve Librarian ALL-of gating, direct-tool anti-patterns, and 5–10× cost signal.
- Preserve General concrete-plan, no-exploration, no-small-task, and cost gating.
- Update tests that snapshot or inspect descriptions/overlay routing.
Out of scope:
- Changing public tool names or parameter schemas.
- Moving hard gates out of tool descriptions.

## Shortening Targets
Current approximate description lengths:
- explore: ~330 chars
- oracle: ~310 chars
- librarian: ~750 chars (longest — multiple anti-patterns)
- general: ~680 chars
- reviewer: ~390 chars

Targets after tightening:
- **Each description ≤ 400 chars max.** Librarian and General are the main cuts.
- Remove positive routing prose ("Use when X, Y, Z") that now lives in overlay routing metadata from T-005.
- Preserve and test these exact phrases: `"ALL of these hold"` (Librarian), `"file paths + intended changes"` (General), `"5–10×"` (Librarian + General).
- A char-count assertion in tests (e.g., `assert(desc.length <= 400)`) makes the target enforceable.

## Components Touched
- `src/sub-agents/explore.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/oracle.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/librarian.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/general.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/reviewer.ts`
- `src/sub-agents/__tests__/librarian-gating.test.ts`
- `src/handlers/__tests__/before-agent-start.test.ts`

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- T-005 must be complete so positive routing intent already has a typed metadata home.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Tool descriptions remain the Pi tool-list contract visible to the parent model.
- Positive routing hints should appear in the Bytes overlay via metadata, not duplicated in descriptions.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Over-shortening Librarian or General can weaken strict cost/gating behavior. Preserve negative constraints and cost signals even if positive routing is removed.
- Existing tests may need to be updated carefully without removing fixture coverage for direct-tool anti-patterns.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Description/gating tests pass and still assert Librarian and General strict gates.
- Overlay tests prove concise positive routing hints are still visible via metadata.
- Tests enforce max-length target: `description.length <= 400` for each builtin delegate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each builtin delegate description ≤ 400 chars (enforced by test assertion).
- Phrases preserved: "ALL of these hold" (Librarian), "file paths + intended changes" (General), "5–10×" (both).
- Description/gating tests pass with Librarian and General strict gates intact.
- Overlay tests prove positive routing hints are visible via metadata.
close_reason: Implemented and verified

title: Implement artifact capture core module
description:
## Objective
Create src/sub-agents/artifacts.ts with the core artifact persistence logic: resolveArtifactDir(), captureArtifact(), buildMetadataHeader(), cleanupArtifacts(), and constants (MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES=512KB, MIN_ARTIFACT_CHARS=1024, RETENTION_DAYS=7).

## Context
When sub-agent output exceeds MAX_RETURN_CHARS (24,576), boundReturnContent() truncates the middle. Artifact capture persists the full redacted output to disk so the parent can read it later. This is opt-in and conservative by default.

## Scope
In scope:
- Resolve artifact directory: $PI_AGENT_DIR/blackbytes/artifacts/sub-agents/<YYYY-MM-DD>/, fallback to ~/.pi/agent/blackbytes/artifacts/... when PI_AGENT_DIR unset
